races.title: State Assembly, District 7
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Amy L. Slavensky
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 7. Spent about 40 years in California public schools as a teacher, principal and superintendent, including Amador County Unified School District, and was deputy superintendent at San Juan Unified School District. Holds a Ph.D. in educational leadership.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Nurses Association, the California Teachers Association, California Young Democrats and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Amy Slavensky holding elected office, so there is no voting record to report. We found no documented actions on the issues in our platform. Her only stated positions on housing are a pledge to cut red tape that blocks housing production and to speed up affordable housing. She has not been recorded taking a position on data centers or other development projects. We found nothing on homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. Her campaign site's priorities page lists topic headings such as Housing, Public Safety and Climate & Environment, but the text under them was not available, so we could not read her detailed positions. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. Her birth and upbringing details come only from her own campaign site.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign site says she was born and raised in Fair Oaks and Carmichael, in District 7, attended public schools there, and still lives in an unincorporated community of the district.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: About 40 years in California public education as a teacher, principal, superintendent of Amador County Unified School District and deputy superintendent at San Juan Unified School District, with 30 years leading schools and school systems and responsibility for district budgets. She has held no legislative office.
qual.why: Long management experience, including district budgets, places her in the middle range. She has no prior legislative service and no law or policy-staff career on the record, so she does not reach the high range.
qual.label: Long management experience, including district budgets, places her in the middle range. She has no prior legislative service and no law or policy-staff career on the record, so she does not reach the high range.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says public school teachers and staff should be paid "what they deserve." It gives no figure and takes no stated position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she was born and raised in Fair Oaks and Carmichael, in District 7, attended public schools there, and still lives in an unincorporated community of the district.

cands.name: Josh Hoover
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 7 (Sacramento County suburbs) since December 2022. Previously spent 11 years as a legislative aide, including as chief of staff to Assemblymember Kevin Kiley, and served on the Folsom Cordova Unified School Board. Holds a UCLA bachelor's degree and a USC master's in public administration.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the Republican Party of California and Reform California among his 2026 endorsements.

His campaign site says he is endorsed by law enforcement groups including PORAC, the California Police Chiefs Association, CCPOA, the Sacramento County Deputy Sheriffs Association, the Folsom Police Officers Association and the Sacramento Police Officers Association.

His campaign site says he is endorsed by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, NFIB, the Sacramento Metro Chamber of Commerce, the Sacramento Hispanic Chamber of Commerce and the Folsom Chamber of Commerce.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was raised or when his adult residence in California began. The pages reviewed did not include bill-level records of what he sponsored or did in office, so we could not document his actions on property taxes, land buyers, growth, immigration, guns, abortion or teacher pay. We found no stated position from him on data centers or on development, and no documented controversies. His campaign-site claims about Ryla's Law and endorsements are his own statements, not independently confirmed.

local.label: Roots 40: Wikipedia says he was born in Folsom, California; his upbringing is not documented in the pages reviewed, and the record shows him as an adult in California (UCLA and USC degrees, 11 years as a legislative aide to California Assembly members, Folsom school board, Assembly since 2022, living in Folsom).

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Member of the California State Assembly since December 2022 (re-elected 2024); 11 years as a legislative aide, including chief of staff to Assemblymember Kevin Kiley; former Folsom Cordova Unified School Board member; master's degree in public administration.
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus a long legislative-staff and public-policy career, and earlier local elected office, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: Prior legislative service plus a long legislative-staff and public-policy career, and earlier local elected office, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee seats were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he believes California can fix education by putting students first, empowering parents, providing school choice and restoring local control.

back-police-order.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he opposes soft-on-crime policies, has supported law enforcement, advocated for more school police officers, and introduced Ryla's Law to close loopholes that let child abusers out of jail early.
